messages:
sophie (SRE): Heads-up — ticket CS-8821, customer acme.ai seeing intermittent 502s to hosted inference since about 08:10 UTC. They report 'handshake timeout' and errors spike when we do cert rotation window.
raj (Support): Got the logs from the customer. Root cause unclear. They call https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate. Curl shows TLS handshake timing out sometimes.
carlos (CustOps): Customer says it started right after our cert rotation at ~08:05. They have a steady stream of requests (bursty). They pasted their client output:
```
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwoodinference.com (35.201.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS handshake timeout
* Operation timed out after 10002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```
raj (Support): They are behind corporate firewall, but their traceroute doesn't show anything odd. They tried from two locations and see same pattern.
emily (Eng-Infra): Can we confirm if cert rotation job rolled to all edge POPs? deploy-bot, show job id and status.
deploy-bot: rota-job-2026-04-07-08:05 — status: completed, 95% success on edges, 5% retrying. See /ops/rotations/rota-job-2026-04-07 for traces.
ops-bot: Notified dns-service: some resolvers reported SERVFAIL during rotation window.
sophie (SRE): Ok suspect interplay between cert rotation and resolver flaps. If a resolver returns SERVFAIL, some clients see transient TLS handshake failures (SNI mismatch or missing cert chain). Need repro. Raj, can you get a pcap from customer or have them run a curl with --verbose and --connect-to?
raj (Support): Asked customer for `curl -v --max-time 10 https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate` and `dig +short api.redwoodinference.com @8.8.8.8` and `@their-resolver`. They returned two different IPs depending on resolver.
carlos (CustOps): They also attached `dig +trace` — shows an intermediate resolver returning SERVFAIL intermittently, TTLs low (30s). Looks like a flaky authoritative cache path.
emily (Eng-Infra): Can reproduce partial failures from our side when forcing use of the flaky resolver in testing. Symptoms: TLS handshake stalls waiting for server's CertificateVerify, then client times out. Likely path: resolver returns different A records mid-rotation causing SNI/cert chain mismatch on some edge nodes.
sophie (SRE): Repro notes for eng: run a looped curl/openssl s_client to the two IPs in rotation, inspect cert chains. Example repro command we used:
```
for i in $(seq 1 40); do timeout 5 curl -v --resolve api.redwoodinference.com:443:35.201.12.34 https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate || true; sleep 0.5; done
```
observed ~7% handshake timeouts on the flaky IPs.
emily (Eng-Infra): Looks like our OCSP stapling on a subset of nodes timed out when contacting the OCSP responder during the rotation; combined with resolver flaps we saw cert chain delivery fail on some edges. Opening infra ticket INFRA-4987.
sophie (SRE): Action items: 1) Support: ask customer to add client retry/backoff for 502/504; suggest switching to alternate resolver (8.8.8.8) as short-term mitigation. 2) Eng-Infra: INFRA-4987 to patch OCSP timeout and backoff during rotation. 3) Ops: re-run rotation with staged rate-limited rollout for affected POPs.
raj (Support): Sent workaround note to customer: enable retries with exponential backoff and fallback resolver, and we gave ETA for follow-up. They confirmed temporary patch helped reduce errors.
carlos (CustOps): Customer also asked about billing — they saw many failed requests still billed. Raj: we agreed to audit their invoice and credit failed requests during the incident window.
ops-bot: Re-run scheduled rotation: rota-job-2026-04-07-retry queued (staggered 30s per POP).
emily (Eng-Infra): Patch deployed in canary (OCSP timeout reduced and async stapling retried). Monitoring shows TLS handshake success rate back to baseline after canary.
sophie (SRE): Closing loop notes: root cause = combination of resolver SERVFAIL spikes + OCSP stapling timeouts during cert rollout that caused a subset of edge nodes to present incomplete chains; clients with strict timeouts saw handshake failures -> manifested as 502/504 to customers. Mitigation = engine change (INFRA-4987) + ops rollout policy change.
raj (Support): Marking ticket CS-8821 as escalated/resolved pending billing adjustment and customer confirmation.
carlos (CustOps): Customer acknowledged the credit and will re-run their load tests tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
